column3: Links alliance with deniers to self-incurred blame, divine displeasure, and enduring punishment.
Directly names assigning another deity alongside Allah, clarifying the shirk named in 9:17.
Connects denial of faith with the nullification of deeds, extending 9:17's stated outcome.
Sets a contrary mosque relation: blocking remembrance and seeking ruin rather than rightful maintenance.
Immediately specifies the faith, prayer, giving, and fear-of-Allah profile of those who maintain mosques.
Adds a judgment image for nullified deeds, though its V12 connection is contrast-only.
Reiterates nullified deeds and lack of helpers without adding a mosque or self-witness dimension.
Immediately tests whether service to pilgrims and mosque maintenance can equal faith and striving; it cannot.
Offers a compact witness motif that can parallel 9:17's self-testimony, without localizing its subject.
Extends the boundary around mushrikin after their fire-destiny becomes clear.
Continues the nearby reward sequence but adds little to the eligibility question in 9:17.
Supplies a witness-and-witnessed frame that can sit beside self-testimony in 9:17.
Places dealings with mushrikin at al-Masjid al-Haram under covenant fidelity, adding a nearby legal boundary.
The mutual waiting scene does not clarify mosque maintenance, shirk, self-testimony, or nullified deeds.
Broadens imarah into responsibility for inhabiting and sustaining a place under sole worship of Allah.
Joins al-Masjid al-Haram, kufr, exclusion from it, nullified deeds, fire, and enduring punishment.
Continues the immediate comparison by ranking faith, migration, and striving above the claimed service.
Supplies a stated cause for nullified deeds in rejection of what Allah sent down.
Pairs denial of signs and the final meeting with nullified deeds and recompense for action.
Establishes a later access boundary for mushrikin at al-Masjid al-Haram and addresses the material concern it raises.
The inhabited house image may resonate with imarah, but it supplies no qualifying criterion.
Only repeats the kufr-fire-endurance outcome already explicit in 9:17.
Nearby mobilization language does not directly explain who may maintain mosques.
Provides comprehensive divine witnessing, a parallel frame for the self-testimony in 9:17.
Adds another nullified-deeds case but is redundant after the earlier, closer instances.
Connects maintained prayer with a witnessed dawn recitation, supporting the living-practice side of imarah.
Its nullified-deeds example is relevant only generally; the supplied V12 route is contrast-only.
Uses earlier communities to connect worldly indulgence with nullified deeds in this surah's wider argument.
Continues the nearby reward outcome but does not further define the boundary in 9:17.
The witness motif is general and adds little after stronger self-witness cards.
Directly combines false devotion, self-witness of kufr, and the disappearance of invoked associates.
Nearby punishment of deniers belongs to the context but does not clarify mosque maintenance.
Another nullified-deeds formulation, with only contrast V12 evidence and no mosque relation.
Shares the fire-and-endurance consequence but adds no qualifying relation.
Prayer, giving, and obedience after a lapse offer a practice-centered counterpart to 9:18's criteria.
Links following what angers Allah and disliking His pleasure to nullified deeds.
Contrasts Allah-centered allegiance with alternative patrons, framing the direction of kufr in 9:17.
Nearby warning against kinship loyalty when kufr is preferred adds a competing-allegiance boundary.
The phrase about present sons does not materially clarify the focus verse.
Longevity seeking and divine sight add only a distant consequence frame.
Suspended judgment adds procedural openness but not a criterion for mosque maintenance.
Treats concealment of testimony as grave wrongdoing, sharpening the ethical weight of witness language.
Pairs signs in horizons and selves with Allah's all-encompassing witnessing.
Rejoins prayer, giving, and certainty of the final life, closely matching 9:18's positive profile.
States that shirk nullifies deeds, though the linked V12 route is contrast-only.
Contrasts extensive settlement-building with a self-wronging end, qualifying imarah by moral orientation.
Nearby competing loves, commerce, and dwellings show how material attachments can displace Allah's way.
Portrays standing by testimonies as a sustained practice, useful beside 9:17's self-testimony.
Links dwelling and faith with welcoming, self-preference, and overcoming inner avarice.
Nearby reluctance to mobilize is contextual but does not directly interpret 9:17.
Community witness is relevant in theme but distant from the mosque-maintenance criterion.
Affirms one deity and straightness toward Him while warning mushrikin.
The brief command does not add a clear relation to the focus verse.
Connects kufr, blocking Allah's way, and opposition after guidance with nullified deeds.
Distinguishes coercion from an opened commitment to kufr, refining the kufr category in 9:17.
The warning that numerical abundance does not suffice is nearby but indirect.
Frames the messenger as a witness over a community, providing a public counterpart to self-witness.
Rejects taking angels and prophets as lords, directly clarifying another-deity language.
The call to strive is nearby context but supplies no mosque or witness criterion.
Its covenant and collective self-reference only loosely parallel self-testimony.
Contrasts a spoken claim of faith with concealed and continuing kufr.
The scene of bewilderment does not clarify the focus verse.
Explicitly makes shirk destructive of deeds even in a guided prophetic setting.
Joins justice, sincere religion for Allah, and orientation at every mosque as a direct positive counterpart.
Nearby repentance adds a possible later turn but not the focus verse's stated qualification.
Prohibits concealing testimony and locates the resulting sin in the heart.
Divine witnessing of judgment is only a broad thematic parallel.
Nearby refusal to strive supplies context but no direct account of mosque maintenance.
Makes bodily members witnesses against their persons, strongly extending the self-testimony motif.
Its every-mosque instruction concerns adornment and restraint, not the eligibility boundary.
Combines guided leadership, good works, prayer, giving, and worship in a communal maintenance profile.
Shows deeds can be nullified through a failing in relation to the messenger, adding another integrity boundary.
Defines righteousness through faith, giving, prayer, charity, covenant, and endurance rather than mere orientation.
Continues the local sequence but moves to a different legal-political relation than 9:17.
Models testimony limited to what is known, a useful constraint on reading self-witness.
Combines striving, messenger-and-community witnessing, prayer, giving, and holding fast to Allah.
Nearby pursuit of discord is contextual but does not specify the focus verse's terms.
Allah as sufficient witness is a broad parallel, weaker than the self-witness cards.
The request for good and protection from fire supplies only a general outcome contrast.
The reciprocal command to act from one's position does not clarify 9:17.
Its witness relation depends on an unresolved referent and is distant from the focus.
Relates ritual completion and eligibility around al-Masjid al-Haram, but not the shirk boundary.
The request to bring a clear thing has no material interpretive link to 9:17.
Shows that a charge needs witnesses and that failure of that route redirects blame to the speakers.
Combines knowledge of unseen and witnessed reality with transcendence over shirk.
The reward statement does not materially clarify the focus verse.
Makes a person's own repeated testimony legally weighty when external witnesses are absent.
Reiterates the mushrikin-fire-endurance outcome without adding the mosque-maintenance relation.
Dependence on Allah is thematically compatible with worship but adds no direct criterion.
Returns deeds to the knower of unseen and witnessed reality, but only as a general accountability frame.
The sign in selves loosely echoes self-reference without clarifying testimony or kufr.
Failure to restrain a committed wrong adds a communal-integrity concern relevant to public maintenance.
Speaking about Allah without knowledge is a distant caution, not a direct focus link.
The reproaching self only loosely relates to self-testimony.
Links denial of revelation with mishandling and concealment of scripture, refining a kufr-related posture.
The worldly-growth image does not materially clarify mosque maintenance or self-witness.
Family support and nursing rules do not materially clarify the focus verse.
The favorable enduring dwelling is only a generic outcome contrast.
Inheritance allocation does not materially clarify the focus verse.
The general affirmation of truth and non-wronging adds no specific focus relation.
Connects the House's purification with its worshipping uses, supplying a direct positive maintenance frame.
The raising of the House's foundations adds a construction-side parallel to imarah, without the focus verse's exclusion criterion.
Shows that outward charitable action can be invalidated by its manner and intention, qualifying the works language in 9:17.
Adds non-acceptance and final loss for a religious orientation other than Islam.
Marks association with Allah as a distinct, grave boundary while leaving other wrongs differently situated.
Reiterates the association-forgiveness boundary already supplied more directly by 4:48.
Directly joins shirk with exclusion from paradise and fire, sharply framing 9:17's outcome.
Explicitly has people testify against themselves that they were disbelievers.
Provides a primordial self-testimony scene, extending the witness vocabulary without the kufr judgment of 9:17.
Identifies prevention from al-Masjid al-Haram and denies guardianship except to the muttaqun.
Qualifies the mushrikin's practice at the House, making ritual presence alone insufficient.
Names a mosque established for harm, kufr, division, and hostile positioning, directly testing the integrity of mosque-building.
Contrasts that mosque with one founded on taqwa and describes the people fit to stand there.
Contrasts a foundation on taqwa and divine pleasure with a foundation on a collapsing edge.
Extends the harmful-mosque account by locating its construction as a continuing source of inner doubt.
Pairs a sacred locality with a plea for protection from worshipping idols.
Places descendants near the sacred House specifically in relation to establishing prayer.
Offers an image of deeds dispersed under disbelief, adding a non-identical nullification parallel.
Makes a person sufficient against himself in the accounting scene, a close self-evidence counterpart.
Describes lost worldly striving that is nevertheless thought to be good, directly deepening the nullified-deeds issue.
Pairs worship of one Lord with the command not to associate anyone in that worship.
Links exclusive divinity with establishing prayer for remembrance.
Connects denial and obstruction from al-Masjid al-Haram with a stated sacred-space relation and punishment.
Links the House's purification with exclusive worship practices around it.
Includes mosques among places where Allah's name is much mentioned, supporting their worship-purpose dimension.
Makes tongues, hands, and feet witnesses against their people, extending embodied self-testimony.
Describes houses Allah permitted to be raised and His name remembered in, a direct positive counterpart to mosque maintenance.
Qualifies those worshippers by undistracted remembrance, prayer, giving, and fear of the accounting day.
Uses an image of apparently substantial deeds failing before Allah, a parallel to habita without duplicating its wording.
Depicts deeds being rendered scattered dust, adding a consequence parallel to nullification.
Links established prayer to restraint from indecency and wrong, supporting integrity in worship practice.
Names shirk as great wrongdoing in a direct parental teaching scene.
Makes mouths sealed while hands and feet testify to what people earned.
Adds hearing, sight, and skins as witnesses against their persons; it directly completes the following listed card.
Connects denial and prevention from al-Masjid al-Haram with blocked sacrificial access.
Depicts Allah recounting forgotten deeds and being witness over all things.
Commands movement from trade toward the Friday prayer call, supporting priority of communal worship over commerce.
Declares the mosques to belong to Allah and forbids invoking anyone alongside Him there.
States the human being is insight against himself, a compact counterpart to self-testimony.
Combines sincere devotion to Allah, prayer, and giving in a concise positive worship criterion.
Warns about those who pray while neglecting the prayer, qualifying visible ritual by its actual integrity.
Names showing off, adding an intention-based counterpoint to visible religious practice.
